newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW says H1 deliveries climb around 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: BMW says H1 deliveries climb around 10 pct.

text.p: German luxury carmaker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) said on Thursday deliveries climbed 10 percent in the first half of 1997 to around 350,000 units and it grabbed a larger share of the German car market.

BMW, which has faced a tough battle with rival Audi AG in Germany, said it boosted its market share there to 6.5 percent during the first half of the year from 6.1 percent during the same period a year ago.
BMW's success came despite a weak German market.
The company said registrations of new BMW group cars here climbed three percent to over 120,000 units while at the same time the overall market shrank by three percent.
According to a BMW statement, the U.S. provided the carmaker with its fastest growth with registrations there climbing 25 percent to 62,000 units.
In Japan, another important market, BMW registrations climbed 16 percent to 19,000 units and in Britain registrations climbed 9 percent to 30,000 units.
Strong demand for BMW branded cars comes on the back of demand for its 5-Series executive-class saloon.
The mainstay of its fleet, the 3-Series, has seen demand flag somewhat with a new version of the model in the pipeline and customers putting off purchases in order to have the latest model version.
BMW said it will release a more detailed account of its first half results next week.
